hints: Start from the definition of stress used for a stretched wire: stress $= \frac{force}{cross\text{-}sectional\ area}$ so its unit must be $\text{N}$ divided by $\text{m}^2$.
Write $1\ \text{N}$ in base units as $1\ \text{kg m s}^{-2}$ and then divide by $\text{m}^2$ to get the base unit for stress.
Check each option against $\text{N m}^{-2}$: $\text{N m}^{-1}$ is force per length and $\text{N m}$ is force times length, so only one base-unit option matches.
walkthrough: Recall the definition needed here: stress $= \frac{F}{A}$, where $F$ is tensile or compressive force and $A$ is cross-sectional area.
Therefore the unit of stress is the unit of force divided by the unit of area: $\frac{\text{N}}{\text{m}^2} = \text{N m}^{-2}$, also called the pascal.
Expand the newton into SI base units using $F = ma$: $1\ \text{N} = 1\ \text{kg m s}^{-2}$.
Divide by $\text{m}^2$: $1\ \text{N m}^{-2} = 1\ \text{kg m s}^{-2}\text{m}^{-2} = 1\ \text{kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}$.
Compare with the options: $\text{N m}^{-1}$ is force per length and $\text{N m}$ is moment or energy, while $\text{kg m}^{-2}\text{s}^{-2}$ has one power of $\text{m}$ too many.
Hence $\text{kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}$ is the correct base-unit form. This is option A.

options.A: Stress is force per area, $\text{N m}^{-2}$, which equals $\text{kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}$ in base units.
options.B: This has an extra $\text{m}^{-1}$ factor and corresponds to force per volume, not force per area.
options.C: $\text{N m}^{-1}$ is force per length, the unit for surface tension or spring constant, not stress.
options.D: $\text{N m}$ is force times distance, the unit for moment or energy, not stress.
